# Windowmac

> Windowmac is a free, open-source (MIT) window manager for macOS. Hold the Option key, flick the mouse toward where a window should go, and let go: the window snaps to a half, third, two thirds, quarter, maximised, centred or another display. No account, no tracking, and the app never connects to the internet.

Key facts:
- Site: https://www.windowmac.app/
- Platform: macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon and Intel.
- Price: free and open source under the MIT license.
- Permission: Accessibility only (macOS requires it for any app that moves other apps' windows).
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://www.windowmac.app/install.sh | bash`, or download the latest release from GitHub.
- Source: https://github.com/iam8uman/windowmac (by Suman Sharma, made in Nepal).
- Not on the Mac App Store and not yet notarized, so macOS shows a first-launch warning; System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway allows it.

## How it works

1. Hold Left Option. A ring appears under the cursor.
2. Flick the mouse toward where the window belongs. An outline shows where it will land; clicking cycles half, third and two thirds.
3. Release and the window snaps into place. Esc or right-click cancels.

## Features

- Layouts: halves, thirds, two thirds, quarters, maximise, almost maximise, centre, and custom layouts.
- Screens: send a window to the next or previous display; it keeps its layout.
- Strip (new in 1.2): hold Option and press S to line up every window on a screen as sideways-scrolling columns.
- Stash: tuck a window behind the screen edge and push the cursor against the edge to bring it back.
- Resize and nudge any edge, and undo a window's last positions.
- Keyboard shortcuts while holding Option: arrows for halves/thirds, Return to maximise, C to centre, 1-4 for quarters, [ and ] for screens, Z to undo. Every key can be changed.
- Automation: every action has a windowmac:// link, for example `open -g "windowmac://action/right-half"`, usable from scripts, Shortcuts and Raycast.
- Settings: trigger key (Left Option, Right Option or Globe), ring size, shape and colour, window gaps, animation speed, and apps to ignore.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.windowmac.app/): What Windowmac does, an interactive in-browser demo, layouts, shortcuts, install steps and FAQ.
- [Install](https://www.windowmac.app/#install): The one-line installer and the first-launch steps.
- [FAQ](https://www.windowmac.app/#faq): Price, permissions, typing with Option held, customisation, automation, updating and uninstalling.

## Related apps by the same developer

- [Slidemac](https://www.slidemac.app/): Turns the edges of a Mac trackpad into sliders for volume, brightness, app switching and keyboard light.
- [Screenmac](https://www.screenmac.app/): Native macOS screenshot and screen recording app with annotation and redaction.
